Single-omics survival analysis

Source: vignettes/single-omic-analysis.Rmd
single-omic-analysis.Rmd
library(Omics2Surv)

Introduction

This vignette walks through a complete single-omics survival analysis workflow, from data acquisition to patient stratification and functional enrichment. As a working example we use the TCGA-KIPAN cohort (Pan-Kidney Cohort), retrieving RNA-seq, copy number variance (CNV) and DNA methylation data together with the corresponding clinical information.

Although three omics layers are downloaded and assembled into a single MultiAssayExperiment (MAE), in this vignette each omic is modeled independently, one at a time. For a workflow that combines multiple omics into a single predictive model, see the companion vignette("multi-omic-analysis").

Data acquisition & exploration

We start by retrieving the omics and clinical data from LinkedOmics for the TCGA-KIPAN cohort.

KIPANRNA_link = retrieve_linkedomics_data("TCGA-KIPAN","RNAseq (HiSeq, Gene level)")

KIPANCN_link = retrieve_linkedomics_data("TCGA-KIPAN", "SCNV (Gene level, Thresholded)")

KIPAN_Meth_link= retrieve_linkedomics_data("TCGA-KIPAN", "Methylation (Gene level, HM450K)")

KIPANClin_link= retrieve_linkedomics_data("TCGA-KIPAN", "Clinical")

Exploration

Before any modeling step, it is good practice to explore the data structure. explore_pca() performs a principal component analysis on the RNA-seq data and relates the resulting components to a set of clinical/metadata variables.

data_expl= explore_pca(KIPANRNA_link, KIPANClin_link, 
  metavars = c("histological_type", "gender", "radiation_therapy", "race", "ethnicity"))

data_expl$eigencorplot

Data preselection

Optional splitting

The cohort is split into a training and a test set. The same split is shared across all omics layers so that the same patients end up in the training set (and the same patients in the test set) for every layer.

KIPAN_split = split_train_test(
  omics_list     = list(mRNA = KIPANRNA_link,
                        CNV  = KIPANCN_link, methyl = KIPAN_Meth_link),
  clinical_data  = KIPANClin_link
)

Variable screening

Each omic is preprocessed and screened on the training set only, to avoid information leakage from the test set. Here RNA-seq features are selected in an unsupervised fashion based on highly variable genes, CNV features are selected based on sparsity, and methylation features are selected based on interquartile range (IQR).

KIPAN_RNA_train=prepare_RNA(KIPAN_split$train_list$mRNA,   KIPAN_split$train_clinical,method = "unsupervised", unsupervised_method= "A", hvg_threshold = 5)
KIPAN_CNV_train=prepare_CNV(KIPAN_split$train_list$CNV,   KIPAN_split$train_clinical,method = "unsupervised", unsupervised_method = "sparsity", top_n_features = 800)
KIPAN_Meth_train=prepare_methyl(KIPAN_split$train_list$methyl,   KIPAN_split$train_clinical, method="unsupervised", unsupervised_method = "IQR", hvg_threshold = 5)

The same features selected on the training set are then applied to the test set with prepare_test_SE(), so that train and test share an identical feature space.

KIPAN_RNA_test= prepare_test_SE(KIPAN_split$test_list$mRNA,   KIPAN_RNA_train)
KIPAN_Meth_test= prepare_test_SE(KIPAN_split$test_list$methyl,  KIPAN_Meth_train)
KIPAN_CNV_test= prepare_test_SE(KIPAN_split$test_list$CNV,   KIPAN_CNV_train)
omics_train = list(mRNA=KIPAN_RNA_train, CNV=KIPAN_CNV_train, meth= KIPAN_Meth_train)

omics_test = list(mRNA= KIPAN_RNA_test, CNV= KIPAN_CNV_test, meth= KIPAN_Meth_test)

MAE building with 3 omics

The preprocessed omics and the clinical data are assembled into a MultiAssayExperiment object, separately for the training and the test set.

KIPAN_MAE_train = build_MAE(omics_list = omics_train, KIPAN_split$train_clinical)

KIPAN_MAE_test = build_MAE(omics_list = omics_test, KIPAN_split$test_clinical)

Combine train and test clinical data to inspect the overall cohort, and check the censoring rate of the survival status.

KIPAN_train_clin = as.data.frame(KIPAN_MAE_train@colData)
KIPAN_test_clin = as.data.frame(KIPAN_MAE_test@colData)
KIPAN_all_clin = as.data.frame(rbind(KIPAN_train_clin, KIPAN_test_clin))

censoring_rate(KIPAN_all_clin$status)

display_counts(KIPAN_all_clin,"status")

Single-omics modeling

Even though the MAE contains three omics layers, the models below are trained on one omic at a time (integration = "none"), so that each modality’s predictive performance can be assessed independently.

Penalized regression models

RNA

Four penalized regression models are trained on the RNA-seq data: a Cox LASSO, a Cox Adaptive LASSO, a Cox Elastic Net, and a penalized Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) model.

#cox_lasso
KIPAN_MAE_train = train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "cox_lasso",
  nlambda= 200,
  nfolds= 10,
  seed = 8290
)

KIPAN_MAE_test = predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "cox_lasso"
)
#adaptive lasso
KIPAN_MAE_train = train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "cox_adaptive_lasso",
  nlambda= 100,
  nfolds= 10,
  seed = 8290
)

KIPAN_MAE_test = predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "cox_adaptive_lasso"
)
#elastic net
KIPAN_MAE_train = train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "cox_elastic_net",
  nlambda= 200,
  nfolds= 10,
  seed = 8290
)

KIPAN_MAE_test = predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "cox_elastic_net"
)
#penAFT
KIPAN_MAE_train = train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "aft_pen",
  nlambda= 200,
  nfolds= 10,
  seed = 8290
)

KIPAN_MAE_test = predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("mRNA"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "aft_pen"
)

Methylation

The same four models are trained on the methylation data.

#cox_lasso 
KIPAN_MAE_train = train_pen_reg_models( mae_train = KIPAN_MAE_train, omic_list = c("meth"), integration = "none", model_method = "cox_lasso", nlambda= 200, nfolds= 10, seed = 8290 )

KIPAN_MAE_test = predict_pen_reg_models( mae_pred = KIPAN_MAE_test, mae_train = KIPAN_MAE_train, omic_list = c("meth"), integration = "none", model_method = "cox_lasso" )
#adaptive lasso
KIPAN_MAE_train = train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("meth"),
  integration  = "none",

)

KIPAN_MAE_test = predict_pen_reg_models(

  omic_list    = c("meth"),

)
#elastic net
KIPAN_MAE_train = train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("meth"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "cox_elastic_net",
  nlambda= 200,
  nfolds= 10,
  seed = 8290
)

KIPAN_MAE_test = predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("meth"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "cox_elastic_net"
)
#penAFT
KIPAN_MAE_train = train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("meth"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "aft_pen",
  nlambda= 200,
  nfolds= 10,
  seed = 8290
)

KIPAN_MAE_test = predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("meth"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "aft_pen"
)

CNV

Finally, the same four models are trained on the CNV data.

#cox_lasso
KIPAN_MAE_train = train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("CNV"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "cox_lasso",
  nlambda= 200,
  nfolds= 10,
  seed = 8290
)

KIPAN_MAE_test = predict_pen_reg_models(
  mae_pred     = KIPAN_MAE_test,
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("CNV"),
  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "cox_lasso"
)
#adaptive lasso
KIPAN_MAE_train = train_pen_reg_models(
  mae_train    = KIPAN_MAE_train,
  omic_list    = c("CNV"),
  integration  = "none",

KIPAN_MAE_test = predict_pen_reg_models(

#elastic net

  integration  = "none",

KIPAN_MAE_test = predict_pen_reg_models(

)
KIPAN_MAE_train = train_pen_reg_models(

KIPAN_MAE_test = predict_pen_reg_models(

  integration  = "none",
  model_method = "aft_pen"
)

C-index tables

benchmark_models() collects the concordance index (C-index) achieved by every model trained so far and returns a comparison table. Here we restrict the comparison to the three single-omic datasets.

KIPAN_single= benchmark_models(KIPAN_MAE_train, KIPAN_MAE_test, keep_datasets = c("mRNA","meth","CNV"))

Patient stratification

Using the risk scores from the best performing single-omic model (aft_pen on RNA in this example), patients can be stratified into risk groups and the results visualized with Kaplan-Meier curves, UMAP embeddings, and heatmaps.

KIPAN_strat = patient_stratification(KIPAN_MAE_train, KIPAN_MAE_test,
                               model = "aft_pen",                                modality = "mRNA",
                                 method = "survcutpoint",
                                 plot_scores = TRUE)
plot_km(KIPAN_strat)
plot_umap(KIPAN_MAE_test, KIPAN_strat, model = "aft_pen",
             modality = "mRNA", mae_train = KIPAN_MAE_train, n_neighbors = 10)
plot_heatmap(KIPAN_MAE_test, KIPAN_strat, model = "aft_pen",
             modality = "mRNA", mae_train = KIPAN_MAE_train)

Finally, the genes selected by the model can be tested for functional enrichment.

KIPAN_RNA_en = enrich_features(KIPAN_MAE_train, model = "aft_pen", modality = "mRNA")
plot_enrichment(KIPAN_RNA_en, "GO")
